([[Rockville, Maryland]]) | college = [[College of Charleston Cougars men's basketball|College of Charleston]] (2015–2019) | draft_year = 2019 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 50 | draft_team = [[Indiana Pacers]] | career_start = 2019 | years1 = {{nbay|2019|start}}–{{nbay|2020|end}} | team1 = [[Utah Jazz]] | years2 = 2019–2021 | team2 = →[[Salt Lake City Stars]] | years3 = 2021–2022 | team3 = [[UNICS Kazan|UNICS]] | years4 = 2022 | team4 = [[Greensboro Swarm]] | years5 = 2022 | team5 = [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] | years6 = 2022–2023 | team6 = [[New Zealand Breakers]] | years7 = {{nbay|2022|end}} | team7 = Utah Jazz | years8 = 2023–present | team8 = [[Nagasaki Velca]] | highlights = *[[All-NBA G League Team|All-NBA G League First Team]] ([[2019–20 NBA G League season|2020]]) *NBA G League All-Rookie Team (2020) *First-team All-[[Colonial Athletic Association|CAA]] (2019) *2× Second-team All-CAA (2017, 2018) *Third-team All-CAA (2016) *CAA All-Defensive Team (2017) *CAA Rookie of the Year (2016) }} '''Jarrell Isaiah Brantley''' (born June 7, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Nagasaki Velca]] of the [[B.League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[College of Charleston Cougars men's basketball|College of Charleston Cougars]]. ==College career== As a junior, Brantley averaged 17.3 points and 6.6 rebounds per game and was named to the Second Team All-[[Colonial Athletic Association]].{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Andrew |title=College of Charleston's Jarrell Brantley brings skill, passion and laughs to the Cougars' basketball team |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/college-of-charleston-s-jarrell-brantley-brings-skill-passion-and/article_10ea2c64-1d95-11e8-a293-cf4002544ff0.html |access-date=January 18, 2020 |work=[[The Post and Courier]] |date=March 2, 2018}} He averaged 19 points and 8.4 rebounds per game as a senior, while averaging 1.2 three-pointers per game on a 32.8 percent three-point field goal percentage. He was named to the First Team All-Colonial Athletic Association.{{cite news |title=CofC's Brantley and Riller Earn A Spot On The All-CAA First Team |url=https://www.live5news.com/2019/03/08/cofcs-brantley-riller-earn-spot-all-caa-first-team/ |access-date=January 18, 2020 |work=Live 5 News |date=March 8, 2019}} Brantley finished his career with 1,914 points, which is the third highest in the team's history.{{cite news |last=Miller |first=Andrew |title=Why College of Charleston's Jarrell Brantley could hear his name called at NBA draft |date=June 18, 2019 |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/why-college-of-charleston-s-jarrell-brantley-could-hear-his/article_0e6c6c94-8ece-11e9-87d7-abfb7780fc67.html |access-date=June 21, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Utah Jazz (2019–2021)=== Brantley worked out for several [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] teams after his college season ended, including the [[Boston Celtics]], [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Charlotte Hornets]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], and [[Phoenix Suns]]. Brantley was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the second round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] with the 50th overall pick before being traded to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite news|title=Jazz's Jarrell Brantley: Goes to Utah in Round 2 |work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=June 21, 2019|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-jarrell-brantley-goes-to-utah-in-round-2/|access-date=June 21, 2019}}{{cite web|title=Pacers Trade Draft Rights to Brantley|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-trade-draft-rights-brantley|date=July 21, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 21, 2019}} On July 16, 2019, Brantley was signed to a two-way contract by the Jazz.{{cite web|title=Jazz sign Brantley and Wright-Foreman to two-way contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-brantley-and-wright-foreman-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 17, 2019|date=July 16, 2019}} On October 25, 2019, Brantley made his debut in NBA, coming off from bench in an 86–95 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] with three rebounds, an assist and a block.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160667|title=LeBron scores 32, AD adds 21 in Lakers' 95–86 win over Jazz|date=October 25, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 25, 2019}} On January 15, 2020, Brantley tallied 28 points, eight rebounds and five assists for the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] in a loss to the [[Maine Red Claws]].{{cite news |title=Jazz's Jarrell Brantley: Stays hot with 28 points |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-jarrell-brantley-stays-hot-with-28-points/ |access-date=January 18, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 17, 2020}} On February 11, Brantley flirted with a triple double, contributing 26 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists in a 112–108 overtime win over the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite news |title=Jazz's Jarrell Brantley: Nears triple-double Monday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-jarrell-brantley-nears-triple-double-monday/ |access-date=February 14, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 11, 2020}} On April 13, 2021, Brantley played 22 minutes for the Jazz in a 106–96 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder. He scored 10 points off the bench including 2 for 3 from 3-point range, with 4 rebounds and 1 assist. He also proved the most effective defender against Thunder guard-forward [[Luguentz Dort]].{{cite news|title=Despite limited opportunities, Jazz two-way player Jarrell Brantley has kept his smile and his determination|url=https://www.deseret.com/2021/4/14/22383642/despite-limited-opportunities-utah-jazz-two-way-player-jarrell-brantley-okc-thunder-nba-defense|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=April 14, 2021|access-date=April 23, 2021}} On September 15, 2021, with request from Brantley, he was waived by the Jazz.{{cite web|title=Jazz waive Jarrell Brantley|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waive-jarrell-brantley|website=NBA.com|date=September 16, 2021|access-date=September 16, 2021}} ===UNICS (2021–2022)=== On September 20, 2021, Brantley signed with [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]] of the [[VTB United League]].{{cite web|title=UNICS Inked Jarrell Brantley!|url=https://www.unics.ru/eng/news/?id=unics-inked-jarrell-brantley|website=UNICS.ru|date=September 20, 2021|access-date=September 20, 2021}} Brantley left the team in early 2022 due to the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]].{{cite web|title=Unics Kazan reportedly suing Jarrell Brantley for $250,000|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1316372/unics-kazan-reportedly-suing-jarrel-brantley-for-250000/|website=EuroHoops.com|date=March 4, 2022|access-date=March 5, 2022}} The team sued him for $250,000 and tried to prevent him from signing with an [[NBA G League]] team. ===Greensboro Swarm (2022)=== On March 11, 2022, Brantley was acquired via waivers by the [[Greensboro Swarm]],{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 11, 2022}} playing 10 games and averaging 10.2 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.4 steals.{{cite web|first=Luis|last=Modestti|title=Jarrell Brantley signs at Ponce|url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/news/738555/Jarrell-Brantley-signs-at-Ponce|website=LatinBasket.com|date=April 4, 2022|access-date=April 5, 2022}} ===Leones de Ponce (2022)=== On April 5, 2022, Brantley signed with [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]]. Brantley joined the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=LA Clippers 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612746/clippers |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} ===New Zealand Breakers (2022–2023)=== On July 27, 2022, Brantley signed with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] for the [[2022–23 NBL season]].{{Cite web |title=Breakers Thrilled With Latest Signing |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/breakers-thrilled-with-latest-signing |access-date=July 27, 2022 |date=July 27, 2022 |website=NBL.com.au}} He and his brother Jamaal became the first duo of import brothers to play together in an NBL game.{{Cite web |title=Brantley Brothers Create NBL History |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/brantley-brothers-create-nbl-history |access-date=October 20, 2022 |date=October 20, 2022 |website=NBL.com.au}} He was named the Breakers' Club MVP.{{Cite news |title=Brantley Gets Deserved Recognition at Breakers Awards |url=https://www.nzbreakers.basketball/news/brantley-gets-deserved-recognition-at-breakers-awards |access-date=March 1, 2023 |date=March 1, 2023 |website=nzbreakers.basketball}} ===Return to Utah (2023)=== On March 18, 2023, Brantley signed a 10-day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz Sign Jarrell Brantley to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-jarrell-brantley-to-10-day-contract |access-date=March 18, 2023 |date=March 18, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} He appeared in four NBA games for the Jazz. ===Nagasaki Velca (2023–present)=== On August 1, 2023, Brantley signed with [[Nagasaki Velca]] of the [[B.League]].{{cite web|title=ジャレル・ブラントリー選手 契約基本合意（新規）のお知らせ|url=https://www.velca.jp/news/detail/id=46453|website=Velca.jp|publisher=Nagasaki Velca|date=August 1, 2023|access-date=August 2, 2023|language=Japanese}}
